_about: What changed in each release, in a line each, for the people using BlueStick (Reference -> Release notes). Newest first. kind: new | changed | fixed | before_upgrading. Every release has an entry (tests/test_release_notes.py); scripts/bump-version.py adds an empty one to fill. Why a change was made lives in CHANGELOG.md, not here.

entries.text: The Word report no longer asks Word to rebuild its table of contents on opening, which printed page 1 beside every entry. The entries have no page numbers until you update the table (right-click it: Update field in Word, Update index in LibreOffice); the draft page says so.

The Word report's table of contents now opens as a real table of contents in LibreOffice too: the entries sit inside it and an index update replaces them instead of adding a second table under the first.
The Agents section's address is /agents.
Posture's "where to focus" links to patterns and segments open those pages directly.
Old bookmarks no longer redirect: /dashboard, /test-plans, /executions, /agent-sessions, /insights, /workflows, /ingestion-results and /parse-errors now show "page not found". Update any you keep.
The INGESTION_JOB_TIMEOUT setting is no longer read: if your .env still sets it, rename it to INGESTION_STALL_TIMEOUT.
Agents can list the scans uploaded since a date or time.

The subnet insights and the Pick up queue count a risky service found on an unusual port (Remote Desktop on 3390, for example), as the Hosts list's Exposure column does; a port whose service was identified as something else no longer counts by its number.
Every import now maps its hosts to the project's scope subnets the same way; if that mapping fails, the import still completes.
Deleting a finding with many affected hosts is much faster.
Typing assigned: in the Hosts query now suggests everyone it accepts, including global administrators and former members who still hold hosts.
On Hosts, a row now names the weakness that matched for issue and kind conditions too.
"Not revalidated" beside a port now marks exactly the open ports counted as not in the latest scan.
The search on Collaboration and Portfolio is kept when you go back to the page.
An addendum whose baseline is no longer the latest issued report now tells you to start a new addendum to the latest report.
A Word styles file whose header or footer includes a picture or document from outside the file is refused on upload.
Agents see the same NetExec details and certificate warnings (hostname mismatch, wildcard) as the host inspector.
A two-factor sign-in started before your password was changed or reset has to be started again.
A copy button that could not copy now says so.
A port's conflicting scan results now count toward the host's conflicts everywhere — the Hosts list badge, the inspector, and the Pick up queue — and the inspector lists them.
Comparing scans no longer reports every shared host as a state change when one of the scans (a DNS import, for example) recorded no host state.
A scan's Hosts and Ports tabs list addresses in numeric order (10.0.0.2 before 10.0.0.10).
Operations' blocked-import counts stay correct whichever imports are shown.
A Nessus import that could not write some hosts or findings is now marked partial, counts them as skipped, and appears under Needs attention.
A re-processed import that fails can be retried or started again in another format; it is no longer refused as a duplicate of the original upload.
A Masscan file with a line whose address is not an IP address imports the rest of the file and counts that line as skipped, instead of failing.
An IPv6 address written two ways in Masscan output is one host.
Masscan now records a conflict when it reports a host up that an earlier scan recorded as down, as the other scanners do.
Removing what a very large interrupted import left behind no longer restarts the import worker part way.
Accepting an agent's proposed finding no longer replaces the report text of a finding someone else had just created for the same issue; it asks you to decide it on that finding instead.
Starting remediation deadlines from a large report no longer fails when someone changes a finding's status at the same moment.
Marking a finding on a host "Reported fixed" no longer asks for a retest when the finding was judged a false positive a moment before.
Global administrators told about a pending retest are now told they may record its result.

The host inventory download's Active Findings and Critical Findings columns now match the finding count on the Hosts list: accepted-risk and closed findings no longer count, and a finding recorded on a host and its names counts once.
Drafting with AI no longer holds the database while the model answers, so a slow or local model cannot stall an upgrade or other pages.
The host inventory CSV lists hosts and their services in the same order on every download.
An agent reading a finding is told how many evidence records it has, not only the first 50.
Filtering a scan's hosts by a state that does not exist is refused with an explanation instead of showing no hosts.
Filtering evidence or findings by a host, finding, test or session that is not in the project says it was not found instead of showing an empty list.
A scan upload from someone who cannot upload to the project (a viewer, a non-member, a signed-out session) is refused at once, before the file is sent to the server.
Removing a project member also removes them as the owner of the project's sites.
Two administrators removing each other from a project at the same moment can no longer leave it with no administrator.
A note posted in a host's discussion no longer disappears when the host is refreshed at the same moment.
Changing your own role or removing yourself from a project on the Portfolio members sheet now updates what you can do straight away, without a reload.
Reopening the command palette always starts with an empty search.
A paged list you have emptied goes back to its first page.
A download the server refuses now says why, instead of a generic error.
Signing in after a session expires during an upload returns you to the page you were on.
Opening an archived project from Oversight no longer shows another project's Operations; you are told it cannot be opened.
A mistyped review status in a Hosts link is now reported, rather than silently showing every host.
A record address that is not a valid id now says not found, instead of opening the wrong record or loading for ever.
The retired "watching" review state is no longer accepted as a Hosts filter; a saved view or link that uses it shows an error until it is edited.
A saved Oversight link that filters by the old project status in_progress shows an error; choose Active instead. Scripts that set a project's status to in_progress must send active.

Scripts that call the old agent reads /agent/project, /agent/dashboard, /agent/hosts, /agent/hosts/{id}, /agent/hosts/{id}/notes or /agent/scans must move to the /agent/assist reads; those six now answer 404.
POST /audit/log is gone: audit entries are recorded by the server only. A script of your own that posted to it must stop.
An agent reading an evidence record's output a few bytes at a time no longer gets stuck repeating the same read at an accented or other non-ASCII character.
Backups now include the logos and other report-template files installed on the server, and a restore puts back any that are missing.
Any analyst on a project can dismiss, retry, keep or cancel any of its imports, including uploads made by an agent; viewers and auditors no longer see the import queue strip.
An administrator who must still change their password, or set up two-factor sign-in, cannot create accounts until they have.
Comments on a finding show previews of the screenshots waiting to be attached, like host notes.
An agent's recent-notes list follows the Collaboration page (newest activity first, with search), and an agent can list names in every state the Names page offers.
A NetExec capture over 100 MB is refused with a request to split it, instead of failing after exhausting memory.
A Word styles file that links to an outside template or picture is refused at upload.
An unknown state filter on a scan's host list or the Names page is refused with a message naming it, instead of an empty list.
HTTPS over TLS 1.2 now works with ECDSA certificates.
The diagnostics bundle no longer includes values from slow database statements, or a numeric password from your settings.
Resetting a user's two-factor sign-in now signs them out everywhere, not only their agents.
System settings lists every user account, a page at a time, with the total in the heading.
The installation can no longer be left without an active administrator by two admins demoting or deactivating each other.
An agent session started by an administrator who is not a project member ends once they lose the administrator role, and its key does not work again if they rejoin.
A correction an agent makes to a host's operating system is kept when the host is scanned again.
Accepting an agent's proposed finding attaches the test result it cites, so the test no longer offers to create a second finding.
Undoing an endpoint removal always keeps a retest that was asked for; marking it remediated still needs the retest's result.
Saving a finding's report text no longer overwrites a section a colleague changed while you were editing.
A screenshot you paste while a comment is posting is no longer lost.
Changing a finding's status twice in quick succession in the host inspector no longer leaves the row showing the older change.
Bulk status changes and assignments say how many findings actually changed, how many already were as asked, and which were skipped.
Opening a notification from another project switches to that project first, and the list shows which project each one is from.
Posture's active-finding counts match the Findings list they open: a finding judged a false positive on every host is no longer counted as active.
Evidence no longer reports a web or SMB/AD gap for a host whose only such port is closed or filtered.
The Hosts list stays fast for hosts with many closed or filtered ports, and the Matched line agrees exactly with the filter.
A host's page still loads when its vulnerability summary cannot be read.
With remediation tracking off, a contact's remediation document can no longer be read through the report downloads.
A report rendered again after an upgrade prints its text exactly as when it was issued.
An XML file that looks like Nessus but is an nmap scan now imports as nmap, and a failed import no longer shows database text as its error.
Very large DNS record CSVs and RDAP lookup files no longer run the import worker out of memory.
A restore refuses a backup made by a newer version before it changes anything, instead of leaving the application unable to start; it can be overridden.
Deploying no longer replaces a certificate issued by your own CA when its key file is missing; it stops and says so.
Retry, Cancel and Dismiss on inventory download jobs can no longer be pressed twice, and the release notes page opens from a malformed link.
A follow-up recorded for an earlier day shows that day in your installation's time zone, and retest notifications ask only people who can record a result.
Back up first. The upgrade stops, changing nothing, if any account, project membership or project holds a role or status BlueStick does not use; the pre-deploy check lists them.
Copy the whole scripts folder: one script is new and an unused one is gone.
Release notes now go back to the start of October 2026, one entry for each version since.
About BlueStick's "What changed in this version" opens on the version the server runs, even when the browser has an older build.
Release notes: Reference lists what changed in each version, and About BlueStick links to the notes of the one you are running.
The host inspector's findings link to their finding page, and closing one asks for the reason right there instead of leaving the page.
A scan's page names the upload batch it came in with; a query that was refused says, in your history, the character where it went wrong.
Promoting or dismissing a scanner observation on every host now reaches every host with that issue, whichever scanner reported it.
An account an administrator creates must choose its own password at first sign-in.
Removing someone from a project hides its notifications from them and ends their agent sessions in it.
A report whose template cannot be filled is refused when you issue it, instead of taking a report number it can never use.
The Scans page's import figures each open exactly the list they count.
Enter in the Hosts list opens the highlighted host after a sort or filter change.
The CVSS score cannot be typed over while a 3.x or 2.0 vector decides it.
Two people changing the same finding at once no longer fail with an error.
Cancelling an import, or a server under heavy load, answers at once instead of hanging.
Names and Posture load faster on large projects; the evidence gap lists come in address order, IPv6 included.
Back up first. Deploy now starts a stopped database itself and stops, changing nothing, when the database holds rows an upgrade cannot accept, listing them.
The Query page can ask about sites, scope, open ports, whether an observation is judged, and a finding's hosts; long answers page on.
Scanner observations show check ids, the highest CVSS, ports and when last seen, with a Judged filter and a highest-CVSS order.
Giving a finding a new owner tells them.
The Scans page keeps one import history: uploads that were not imported are rows in it, with retry and dismiss. The separate Ingestion results view is gone.
A deleted account's host reviews are kept, shown as by "a former member".
Operations moved from /workbench to /operations; old bookmarks to /workbench no longer open.
With remediation tracking off, no remediation alert appears in the bell.
An IPv6 address written two ways is one host, and a Nessus host named only by an unresolved hostname is no longer made a host.
A worker restarted by a rebuild is no longer reported as stuck.
Large draft reports open several times faster.
Back up first, and resume running agent sessions afterwards.
Agents can propose a subnet's site and description; Proposals has a Scope details filter, and "Accept all shown" accepts them together.
Project admins get one notification per agent session for its scope proposals.
Export on the Scope page writes the declared scope (networks, domains, or a CSV the scope upload reads back) instead of the hosts found in it.
Out-of-scope hosts are exported from Hosts: its out-of-scope filter, then Export targets.
An export with nothing in it now says so, and why.
Agents read their key from a small curl config file in their working folder, so they no longer ask you to set an environment variable or restart them.
"Create briefing" on Posture and Patterns makes the Posture briefing: the overview's argument as one light, printable handout.
The old systemic briefing and the per-site Briefing link on Segments are gone.
Compare scans has a "Find a scan" box, so scans older than the newest 200 can be compared.
On Posture, the scanner observations and promoted findings bars share one design.
System settings names each worker replica and says when a worker's memory cannot be read.
An AI draft or connection test against a provider that keeps trickling data now stops after a fixed time.
A report's preview check is much faster on reports with many images.
A finding's History records every edit of its title, severity, owner, score and report text, with "Show before and after".
Agents can replace their own pending proposal, and the Proposals page says which proposal replaced which.
An agent can record evidence about no single host, and reads long output and its guide in pieces.
Any project analyst can rename a finding and edit its report text; deleting it stays with its author or an admin.
In Word reports, the summary tables' links to findings now go to the finding.
A failed backup says why, and the diagnostics bundle is kept even when the folder it was run from cannot be written.
Deploy from the folder the running installation was started from (or one of the same name): deploy and backup now stop when BlueStick runs from another folder.
Agents can read a scan's ports as the scan page's Ports tab lists them.
Global administrators are notified when the uploads disk runs low, the import queue backs up or a worker goes silent, at most once a day each.
An import is stopped only when it stops making progress; a large file no longer fails just for taking a long time.
The INGESTION_JOB_TIMEOUT setting is now INGESTION_STALL_TIMEOUT (30 minutes without progress by default); the old name is still read for now, with a warning.
An agent session's page shows its first call, how long after the start it came, and how many notes it left.
The status script says when the TLS certificate expires, and warns within 30 days.
The remediation contacts and teams lists say when they show only the first part of a longer list.
NetExec, Nikto, RustScan, SMBMap and BloodHound imports skip a record the database refuses instead of failing the whole file.
A deactivated account can no longer be added to a project, and an over-long username or name is refused with a clear message.
A link to a later page of a scan's current hosts opens that page.
A scan's page lists exactly what each tab counts, 50 a page; the Ports tab shows ports as the scan saw them, and the tab and page stay in the address.
The Hosts filters for certificate issues, weak TLS and weak authentication, and the Scans list, are faster on large projects.
Tool activity keeps its project filter in the address, so Back returns to it.
Accepting a host-status proposal while that host is being removed from the finding no longer fails with an error.
Upload folders left behind by an interrupted upload are cleared automatically.
Compare scans is laid out like Posture, with each scan's tool and type and a section per list.
On Compare scans, New hosts and Dropped hosts open exactly those hosts, not every host the scan saw.
Setting up two-factor authentication now asks for your password.
A webhook's test no longer reveals whether a private address answers.
Nessus files with over-long titles or names import, and nmap no longer counts skipped down hosts as processed.
A deeply nested query is refused with a message, and a query refused for a bad Hosts term is kept in your history.
The Query page calls its language a pipe query language.
In a narrower window, a Query history entry's outcome sits under its query.
The Query history table no longer cuts off Remove, and a refusal's reason shows in full.
The Query page keeps your history, refused queries and your agent's included, with Save, Remove and Clear.
Query suggestions offer an answer's columns after stats, the Hosts search terms, and the project's values for a column.
The Hosts page's recent queries keep one entry per query; running an older one moves it to the top.
The hint under an empty Query answer shows its code as code.
On the Query page, where and fields after stats or top work on the answer, for example to keep only groups on more than 5 hosts.
An empty answer to an exact = comparison says how many rows would match ignoring case, and suggests like().
Query orders addresses as addresses, and two search commands on findings must match the same host.
Query errors point at the right column, top takes limit= anywhere, and Run re-runs the query shown.
An observation row's Open goes to its inspector, and the Query CSV's name carries a timestamp.
A query that cannot run can no longer be saved.
A cut values() list and a partial CSV download now say so.
Compare scans is faster and lists its rows in address order.
The Query page and the guides name every dataset it can ask about.
Query can ask about findings, a finding's hosts, web interfaces and names, and each row has Open.
Query answers download as CSV, a grouped answer can be drawn as a chart, and a builder writes a query from pickers.
The Query editor suggests datasets, commands, columns and values as you type.
The Query page's header and its sort reference read correctly.
Inventory → Query: ask pipe-style questions about hosts, ports and scanner observations, group and count them, and open exactly the rows behind each count.
Save a query for yourself or share it with the project.
Previous and Next in the Scanner observations inspector no longer fill the browser history; Back closes it.
Inventory → Scanner observations lists every observation, with an inspector showing its details, references and every host carrying it, with what the scanner printed on each.
The Findings page no longer has an observations view; old links open Scanner observations.
An agent session's page lists everything it proposed, and the Findings page says how many proposed findings are waiting.
Findings your agent proposed now appear under "Mine" on Proposals and in the top-bar count.
The report-text image picker points to the Project images panel.
The executive summary can show the report's own images, inserted or pasted, as the system description does.
The startup warning about the credential encryption key now gives advice that keeps stored credentials readable.
If CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, set it to your current SECRET_KEY value; any other value makes stored provider and scanner credentials unreadable.
Reference has a guide to changing report templates.
"Memory near its limit" in System settings judges each process's own memory, so one large import no longer leaves it red.
A bulk "Reported fixed" sends each person one retest notification, not one per finding.
"Update project defaults…" refuses when the project's value changed since you looked, instead of overwriting it.
A pasted screenshot cancelled before it uploaded no longer comes back, and "Import what the file holds" is offered only while the file is kept.
A retest request stands until its result is recorded or the finding is judged a false positive, and such hosts are on every retest list.
Choosing Remediated on a host awaiting a retest opens the retest dialog.
Undo after removing a host from a finding restores its retest request.
A note's evidence images print together under its text in reports.
A cut-short JSON file containing an invalid byte keeps its complete records.
Revise and Render again are hidden from roles that cannot use them.
A retest still asked for after a host was moved to Still present can be answered with "Record retest…".
A refused "Update project defaults…" re-reads the report, so the current values show.
Moving a host from Retest pending to Still present keeps the retest request; Remediated then needs a recorded retest that found nothing.
"Update project defaults…" no longer reverts a change someone else made to the draft.
A finding judged a false positive no longer shows a verification gap or asks for a retest.
Re-enrolling two-factor authentication quickly no longer refuses the first code.
On Remediation deadlines, the "All" row's counts open their lists.
A finding's affected systems print in address order, and Preview uses the template's own format.
A project with more than 50 analysts and admins and no saved team can open its drafts.
Wrong passwords from one network no longer lock everyone behind it out of password and two-factor changes.
Saving a draft report from a stale page no longer reverts someone else's change.
Testing or using an AI provider no longer reveals whether a host's port is open.
masscan JSON with stray text keeps the records before it, and a host a DNS import created no longer reads "Changed".
Every link on a draft report asks before leaving unsaved changes.
The bell says the true number of unread notifications.
Retests are per host: "Reported fixed" or a request by hand marks the host Retest pending and tells the finding's owner, or every member when it has none.
"Record retest…" on a host's row records what was run and what it showed, and moves the host to Remediated or Still present.
The Findings list's Hosts filter and the Operations lead show the hosts awaiting a retest.
The finding-level Retest status is gone (existing ones become Open, their hosts Retest pending); remediation states read "Awaiting fix" and "Outstanding".
"Reported fixed" with no date is dated today.
Paste a screenshot into the Project images panel to upload it.
A pasted image is no longer lost when the clipboard holds it in an unusual way.
A one-field section of a draft says "Customised for this report" only once.
A draft report is a workspace: Details, Review and Preview & issue, one Save draft, and an action bar that stays in view.
"Update project defaults…" lists a draft's customised details and makes the ticked ones the project's.
A preview says whether it still matches the draft.
The Reports page lists drafts and issued reports; the project's report defaults and the templates have their own pages.
The executive summary is a project report default that every report prints unless it overrides it.
Remediation deadlines gain Total and Remediated columns and a Defect metrics table with the mean days to remediate.
Operations calls out your findings with hosts marked for retest.
A screenshot pasted into the System description is uploaded and placed, and a code block can carry a numbered "Listing" caption.
In Word, the summary of findings links go to the finding, and reports no longer name the scanner on every finding.
Issue and Preview wait while you are editing a project default from a draft.
A revision or addendum keeps a system diagram deleted after the original was issued.
Two first saves of report defaults at the same time no longer fail.
The issued reports list marks the newest "Latest" and a revised one "Superseded", and a draft's line says what it overrides.
The Table button writes an empty caption line, and an auditor's checklist shows no fix links they cannot use.
Only tables written in report text get numbered captions; the template's own tables do not.
The Word report's table of contents is filled even when the file opens in Protected View.
The team and distribution tables no longer break e-mail addresses mid-word.
Table captions print under their tables, in HTML and Word.
Word fills the report's table of contents when the file is opened.
Each draft detail shows one action, with the others in a "⋯" menu; the template's notes are in an info tip.
"Set for the project" puts the caret in its field and cannot save an empty value.
An overridden draft detail can be made the project's default, and a followed one set for the project in place.
"Continue a draft?" tells drafts apart (who started each, when, what it overrides) and can discard them.
A followed detail shows as text, with where it comes from.
One "Before issuing" checklist at the top of a draft, every line leading to its fix.
"New report" offers to continue a draft in progress, and the HTML preview opens in a browser tab.
Every detail of a draft follows the project's report defaults unless the draft overrides it, and says where it comes from.
The author is on the report's title page, the project details table is no longer squeezed, and a finding with no evidence prints no Evidence section.
The Reports list and a report's page update when rendering finishes, and System description images open full size.
System settings' worker health also shows the host's memory and load, each process's memory against its limit, and the database's size and connections.
Uploaded scans, evidence images and reports can be read only by the application, not by other accounts on the host.
The database turns TLS on at every start, so a renewed certificate is picked up by restarting the database.
Deploy checks file ownership and permissions before it writes, explains each problem and offers to fix what it can; no folder is made world-writable any more.
The Executive brief prints the author and a written disclaimer, and the Issue dialog names the template and formats used.
The report defaults say whether the system description, other targets and disclaimer are written.
A table in report text can carry a numbered caption with a "Table:" line.
Findings have an Evidence text section, and the report prints an image's note text before the image.
Upload images on the Reports page and place them in the System description.
A report names its author and can carry its own disclaimer, from the report, the project's defaults or the installation's.
Reorder the assessment team and distribution list; downloads show progress and cannot be started twice.
Word reports no longer print the word CLASSIFICATION in every header and footer.
On Remediation deadlines, a contact's Document is offered with every project shown, and asks which project.
The contact document lists the most urgent first, can be narrowed like the reminder, and warns about findings with no recommendation.
Assigning offers the contacts already in use, and a bulk edit previews the new due dates.
The bell opens a panel of unread notifications where you are.
The Projects count on Remediation deadlines is the rows listed.
A rename or report-text save made while a host change was on its way no longer reverts on the page.
The Admin guide explains the report writing guidance.
Each Findings row says what it still needs before the report (missing report text, an image without a caption, proposals to decide), with a Needs filter.
A draft report lists findings with uncaptioned images, and the Issue dialog counts them.
Operations' findings that need you include your findings with an uncaptioned report image.
An agent can keep its own cut-short upload after asking you.
Every format that can tell it was cut short (nmap, masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, BloodHound, NetExec, RDAP, JSON lines) now fails and offers to import what it holds.
An import says how many hosts it renamed, with a link to them; the scan page marks them and Hosts can filter by "Renamed by".
A JSON file that was cut short fails with a clear message and offers "Import what the file holds".
A DNS import counts the existing hosts it addresses on Scans, the scan's page and Hosts.
Deleting a user ends their agent sessions; the sessions and their work stay listed.
Setting a host's review status needs the analyst role.
Deactivating an account ends its browser and agent sessions, a two-factor code works only once, and repeated wrong passwords are throttled.
Only accounts that can write in a project can set up AI providers, and viewers can no longer read remediation details in agent call logs.
Hosts: bulk actions wait while a new filter loads, and a filter value that names nothing is refused instead of listing every host.
Finding comments past the 100th appear, with "Show earlier comments", and downloads with non-Latin names work.
Back up first. The upgrade stops, changing nothing, if the scope lists one network twice with different descriptions or sites.
Ingestion results' Failed figure says how many are dismissed, with a link to them.
Scans' time column is "Uploaded", with the run time on a second line where it differs.
An agent's note notifies the people it mentions, as a person's does.
Scope's subnet list pages 50 at a time, and ticks carry across the pages of a search.
Switching between Imported scans and Ingestion results no longer flickers.
Back up first.
The Scope page says "outside the scope".
A project has exactly one scope, and it has no name: Segments no longer prints one under each network.
Back up first. The upgrade merges a project's extra scopes and stops, changing nothing, if two of them hold the same network or domain.
Segments, the audit log and Ingestion results use the shared pager, which states the page number.
A finding made by dismissing a scanner observation says so in its history.
A late answer no longer puts an older version of a finding back on the page.
The Scope page's export covers every host its table lists.
Ingestion results is now a view on the Scans page; old links still land there.
Mark a scanner observation as a false positive from the Scanner observations list.
Scanner rows are called scanner observations everywhere, and the bell counts "notifications".
Old notifications about test plans no longer count in the bell.
The Scope page lists every subnet and domain of the project.
Remediation deadlines is offered only to project admins, and a host's or finding's browser tab names it.
Patterns gives a subnet whose only condition is SMB signing or deprecated TLS its own question, not "Mixed weaknesses".
An agent client whose key was refused is told why and what to do, instead of seeing a web server error.
On Scanner observations, Details shows what the scanner wrote (description, remediation, CVSS) above the hosts.
The Scanner observations list pages 50 at a time, and ticks carry across pages.
Delete on a note or comment image is offered only to its uploader or a project admin.
Agent activity's "Load older sessions" has no 1,000-session stop, and a failed load keeps the rows shown.
The state bar beside a finding's Affected hosts appears only when its hosts are in more than one state, and its parts look clickable.
Scanner integrations are shown as a table, and Default credentials keeps vendor, search and page in the address.
An AI provider's API key is no longer kept in the page after saving.
In the report defaults and start-the-clock forms, editing one field no longer freezes the others.
Hosts no longer re-reads its filter options each time you return to the tab.
An agent can see which scanners are configured, and asks you before requesting one scanner's credentials; each request is recorded.
Scanner integrations belong to the installation: every signed-in user sees the list, never its secrets, and global admins manage them.
The pasted session prompt no longer contains scanner credentials.
Back up first. Every scanner integration becomes visible to all users and usable from any project's agent session on request; review Scanner Integrations afterwards.
A finished host review can carry an optional note.
Marking a host Reviewed is one click, and "Reviewed, next unreviewed" moves on; review conclusions are gone.
Posture's "Still needs evidence" measure and the Hosts query word conclusion: are gone.
A bulk Reviewed now counts for "Changed since review" as a single one does.
A saved Hosts view using conclusion: shows an unknown-field error until it is edited.
A host's Tests section opens by itself when there are tests to do.
Start Agent Session no longer asks for a purpose, and the Feedback page has no Source filter.
The top bar's agent badge says it counts the sessions in this project.
In Project settings, editing one field no longer freezes the others, so a teammate's saved change is not overwritten.
